body: The Appellate Division of the Superior Court of New Jersey on October 30, 2026, affirmed a Law Division order dismissing with prejudice a neighboring owner's challenge to approvals for the renovation of the Gottlieb Building, a two-story building erected in 1906 at 641 Arnold Avenue in Point Pleasant Beach's downtown commercial district. The borough's Zoning Board of Adjustment had unanimously approved a restaurant and spa on the first floor and a seven-room hotel on the second. Plaintiff 637 Arnold, LLC owns the adjoining property and shares a lot line with it.

This was the building's second approval. Its prior owners applied in 2020 and in 2021 obtained variance relief for a first-floor marketplace and a second-floor hotel, a use not otherwise permitted in the zone; 637 Arnold opposed that application and lost a prerogative writs challenge to it. The prior owners never started the work and in 2023 sold the property to Arnold Shores, LLC, whose managing member is Hollston Hills, LLC; those two companies and Hollston Realty Group, LLC acted jointly on the new application. In a separate boundary dispute between the two parcels, the Superior Court entered a final order on June 11, 2021, adopting a commissioners' report that corrected the common lot line.

Arnold Shores' 2024 application kept the approved hotel plan and added a restaurant, a permitted use, and a spa, which is not. After hearings on March 7, April 4 and May 30, 2024, at which 637 Arnold objected and the applicants presented testimony from their manager, architect, licensed planner and one of the owners, the Board unanimously approved the project and memorialized it in a June 20, 2024 resolution adopting the planner's testimony. 637 Arnold sued on August 12, 2024, arguing among other things that the public notice was deficient, that the Board did not apply the proper use-variance analysis to the combined uses, that the site plan relied on an invalid survey, and that the proceedings were tainted by bias. After a March 7, 2025 trial, Judge Francis R. Hodgson, Jr. rejected each argument, finding the notice adequate and the survey discrepancy, about a quarter inch, immaterial.

Judges Sabatino and Torregrossa-O'Connor affirmed in an unpublished per curiam opinion, substantially for the trial judge's reasons. The panel added that the Board properly applied the use-variance standard to the combined restaurant, spa and hotel uses and made the required findings that the site is particularly suitable and that the relief would not substantially harm the public good or impair the zone plan and zoning ordinance.

timeline.label: Prior owners obtain variance relief for a second-floor hotel at the Gottlieb Building; 637 Arnold's court challenge to that approval is dismissed
Prior owners sell the building to Arnold Shores, LLC without having built the approved project
Zoning Board memorializes unanimous approval of a ground-floor restaurant and spa with the previously approved hotel use
Law Division dismisses 637 Arnold's challenge with prejudice following trial
